skill.name: marketing-ideas
skill.description: Helps SaaS and software teams choose marketing ideas, growth tactics, and campaign strategies from a library of 140 approaches.
skill.summary: Suggests SaaS marketing ideas based on product, audience, stage, budget, and resources.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Software teams often struggle to choose marketing tactics that fit their stage and resources. This skill turns a catalog of 140 SaaS ideas into focused recommendations with implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Recommends 3 to 5 marketing ideas based on product, audience, stage, budget, and team size.
Organizes 140 SaaS marketing tactics across content, ads, community, email, partnerships, events, PR, and product-led growth.
Explains why each selected idea fits the user context and expected growth goal.
Provides first implementation steps, expected outcomes, and required resources for each recommendation.
Suggests context questions when product, audience, or prior marketing work is unclear.
limitations: Does not execute campaigns, buy ads, send emails, or access marketing platforms.
Does not verify current advertising rules, platform pricing, or legal requirements.
Needs product, audience, stage, budget, and past results for best recommendations.
Provides strategic guidance, not guaranteed performance forecasts or attribution analysis.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Early Growth Channels
use_cases.description: Choose practical channels for a pre-launch or early-stage SaaS product with limited budget and a small team.

use_cases.title: Plan Campaign Experiments
use_cases.description: Turn broad growth goals into focused marketing experiments with clear starting steps and resource needs.

use_cases.title: Find Developer-Led Demand Ideas
use_cases.description: Identify technical marketing tactics such as free tools, public APIs, open source, and developer relations.

prompt_templates.title: Get Starter Ideas
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with basic product context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest 5 marketing ideas for my SaaS product. My product is [product], my audience is [audience], and my stage is [stage].

prompt_templates.title: Match Ideas To Constraints
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with budget and team limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend 3 marketing tactics for [product]. We have [budget], [team size], and need results within [timeline]. Explain why each fits.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Channel Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced channel selection across multiple options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare content, paid ads, community, partnerships, and product-led tactics for [product]. Rank them for our audience, budget, and current traction.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Test Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a structured growth program.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day marketing experiment roadmap for [product]. Include hypotheses, selected tactics, starting steps, expected outcomes, and resources needed.

output_examples.input: We have a developer tool for API testing, a small team, and almost no ad budget.
output: Free tool strategy: build a small public API checker that solves a common workflow pain.
Open source marketing: release a useful helper library that leads developers back to the product.
Developer relations: answer practical questions in communities where API teams already gather.

output_examples.input: Our B2B SaaS has steady traffic, but trials do not activate often enough.
output: Onboarding emails: guide new users to the first meaningful product outcome.
Concierge setup: offer hands-on help to high-value accounts during trial onboarding.
Offboarding flows: learn why users leave and test save offers or pause options.

output_examples.input: We need one campaign idea for enterprise buyers in a crowded category.
output_examples.output: Competitor comparison pages can capture high-intent buyers. Start with honest positioning, proof points, and clear migration guidance.

best_practices: Share product, audience, stage, budget, team size, timeline, and prior results before asking for recommendations.
Ask for a small set of ranked ideas instead of a large unsorted list.
Request implementation steps, expected outcomes, and resource needs for each selected tactic.
anti_patterns: Using every listed tactic without filtering for stage, audience, or budget.
Asking for guaranteed growth results without supplying baseline metrics or constraints.
Treating marketing examples as legal, compliance, or platform policy advice.

faq.question: What kind of products does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is designed for SaaS and software products, especially teams choosing customer acquisition and growth tactics.

faq.question: Can it create a complete marketing plan?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn selected tactics into a practical plan when you provide goals, audience, budget, and timeline.

faq.question: Does it run marketing campaigns for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy, prioritization, and implementation guidance, but it does not access external marketing tools.

faq.question: How many ideas should I ask for?
faq.answer: Ask for 3 to 5 ideas when you want focused recommendations that are easier to evaluate and test.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What context improves the recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide your product, target customer, current stage, budget, team size, timeline, and tactics already tried.
